paragraphs: One-sentence judgment | this occupation is worth further verification only if you are willing to accompany pregnant women through pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period over the long term, can maintain assessment and communication ability within an unpredictable labor rhythm, and accept the continuing requirements of graduate nursing education, midwifery certification, and practice licensure; being drawn to the romantic image of welcoming new life is not enough by itself.

Core output | linking antenatal assessment and fetal monitoring records, labor observation and delivery records, newborn assessment records, medication and procedure records, and health education and follow-up arrangements into a traceable maternity care file: reviewable examination and procedure records, not just the outcome of one delivery.

20—120 minute safe trial | use a fictional case for one off-site exercise: based on the given gestational age, chief complaint, and sign excerpts, write out three antenatal assessment items that must be verified, list two conditions requiring immediate referral or escalation, and write out a patient education outline including postpartum observation key points and breastfeeding guidance. The exercise uses only fictional data, and no examination, delivery, or procedure may be performed on any real pregnant woman or newborn.

First threshold | confirm the licensing and authorization boundary first: who may prescribe medications and tests, who decides on referral or surgery when labor is abnormal, and who bears responsibility for delivery and newborn management. This occupation in the United States requires a registered nurse with graduate nursing education and must meet state registered nurse licensure, midwifery certification, and practice authorization requirements; institutions providing midwifery technical services in mainland China must obtain a Maternal and Infant Health Care Technical Service Practice License, and personnel must pass the county-level health authority assessment and obtain a Maternal and Infant Health Care Technology Assessment Certificate.

Nurse Midwives (O*NET-SOC 29-1161.00, Nurse Midwives) diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birth process independently or within a medical team, and may provide gynecological care for healthy women; this occupation in the United States requires professional graduate nursing education. The work includes: providing antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, or newborn care for patients; monitoring fetal development by listening to fetal heart tones, external uterine measurement, identifying fetal position, or estimating fetal size and weight; recording health history, symptoms, and physical examination findings; performing vital sign, neurological reflex, breast, and pelvic examinations; prescribing medications within the scope permitted by state regulations; ordering and interpreting diagnostic or laboratory tests; developing and implementing individualized health management plans; providing family planning services (including inserting intrauterine devices, dispensing oral contraceptives, and fitting cervical barriers); initiating emergency interventions to stabilize patients; consulting or referring to specialists when the condition exceeds the scope of practice or professional competence; educating patients and families about antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, newborn, or interpregnancy care; writing narrative summaries in the medical record to convey patient information to other healthcare providers; and instructing student midwives, medical students, or residents.

entries: Antenatal and postpartum care | provide antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, and newborn care, educate patients and families about antenatal, postpartum, and newborn care, and develop individualized health management plans.

Fetal and labor monitoring | monitor fetal development by listening to fetal heart tones, external uterine measurement, identifying fetal position, or estimating fetal size and weight, and continuously assess progress and abnormalities during labor.

Examination and diagnosis | perform vital sign, neurological reflex, breast, and pelvic examinations, record health history and physical examination findings, order and interpret diagnostic or laboratory tests, and screen for gynecological diseases and assess mental health status.

Medication and procedures | prescribe medications within the scope permitted by state regulations, provide family planning services (inserting intrauterine devices, dispensing oral contraceptives, fitting cervical barriers, and so on), and initiate emergency interventions to stabilize patients.

Referral and collaboration | consult or refer to specialist physicians when the condition exceeds the scope of practice or professional competence, and write narrative summaries in the medical record to convey patient information to other healthcare providers.

Education, research, and quality | develop practice guidelines for primary women's health care and reproductive-age family care and newborn care, plan and evaluate education programs for nursing staff or medical teams or the community, and conduct clinical research on maternal and infant health, contraceptive methods, and breastfeeding.

Mentoring and guidance | instruct student midwives, medical students, or residents on the birth process, and continuously read literature and participate in professional organizations to keep up with developments in midwifery.

paragraphs: The work covers outpatient clinics, delivery rooms, and inpatient wards: O*NET shows 82% work more than 40 hours per week, 81% make decisions daily, 61% report that decisions are very important to results, and 67% have a lot of decision freedom; 55% have a regular work schedule while 45% do not, related to the unpredictable timing of labor, night standby, and duty arrangements.

Exposure and precision requirements concentrate in clinical contact: O*NET shows 69% exposed to disease or infection daily and 81% wear common protective or safety equipment daily; 78% consider the consequences of error extremely serious, 58% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, and 36% report very high responsibility for the health and safety of others; 48% face time pressure daily, and 52% encounter conflict situations at least weekly.

The O*NET interest code is SI (Social, Investigative); work styles are mainly sincerity, persistence, adaptability, empathy, stress tolerance, self-control, social orientation, cooperation, caution, and integrity; Job Zone 5 (SVP 8.0 and above), and the education survey shows 81% master's degrees, 16% post-master's certificates, and 3% post-bachelor's certificates. These dimensions describe activity preferences and work requirements and cannot be treated as hiring standards, ability assessment conclusions, or career destiny judgments.

The capability focus is maintaining assessment and communication ability within an unpredictable labor rhythm: matching gestational age, chief complaint, signs, and examination results, and stating the criteria for continued observation, further examination, or immediate referral; the ability list is mainly written comprehension, deductive and inductive reasoning, oral comprehension and expression, and problem sensitivity.

Responsibility boundary | in the United States, nurse midwives may prescribe medications and tests within their license and state law authorization, manage deliveries independently or within a team, and refer when beyond scope; in mainland China, providing midwifery technical services requires both institutional licensing and personnel assessment qualification, and specific position duties are determined by institutional rules and competent department provisions.

Nurse midwives should be distinguished from adjacent directions such as obstetricians and gynecologists, registered nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwifery-related technical personnel by the main work object, independent practice authority, and referral boundary, rather than by similarity of job titles.

The comparison objects in this table come from the official tasks of O*NET 29-1161.00 and the official occupation descriptions and current systems of adjacent occupations; this occupation in the United States is a graduate-level midwifery nursing role that may manage deliveries independently or within a team; midwifery technical services in mainland China are subject to both the maternal and infant health care special licensing and nurse practice registration management, with an authority boundary different from surgical intervention positions.

The obstetrician and gynecologist direction may perform surgery and bear final medical decisions for high-risk pregnancy, while this occupation focuses on continuity of care and labor management in normal and low-risk maternity cases and refers when surgery or high-risk management is required; the practice focus of registered nurses and nurse practitioners is nursing execution and comprehensive diagnosis and treatment respectively.

If you want to provide continuity of maternity care and participate in labor management over the long term and complete graduate education, midwifery certification, and practice authorization within the U.S. system, you may continue verifying this occupation; if you would rather handle high-risk pregnancy and surgical intervention, you should choose the obstetrician and gynecologist path.

Name and scope | this occupation corresponds to O*NET-SOC 29-1161.00 (Nurse Midwives), a graduate-level midwifery nursing role in the United States that may manage deliveries independently or within a medical team and provide gynecological care. paragraphs: The key signals of fit for this occupation are: being able to maintain assessment and recording habits within an unpredictable labor rhythm, being able to communicate effectively with pregnant women and families, being able to refer or escalate promptly when something is abnormal, and being willing to take on continuing education and certification requirements; interest and work style labels cannot determine fit.

Interest codes and work styles come from the O*NET 29-1161.00 summary and are exploratory evidence; the fit signals and trial design on this page are editorial synthesis and do not constitute selection standards, ability assessment, or a hiring promise.

Boundary statement | this list cannot replace the institution's special maternal and infant health care technical service standards, obstetric emergency and referral processes, infection control systems, or adverse event reporting systems. The main risks center on: missed antenatal assessment or delayed fetal monitoring interpretation, untimely identification of abnormal labor and referral, medication and procedure verification errors, inadequate newborn resuscitation preparation, infection and body fluid exposure, and missing records and follow-up; control requirements should be tailored to the institutional license scope and position authorization.

The main risks are delayed assessment or monitoring, inadequate response to emergencies such as postpartum hemorrhage, medication and procedure verification errors, inadequate newborn resuscitation preparation, and exposure; control them through applicable monitoring, medication and procedure re-check, emergency drills, and referral systems, with two-person requirements checked against the specific system.

Evidence scope | the risk items come from the tasks and work context of O*NET 29-1161.00 (69% exposed to disease or infection daily, 58% consider precision extremely important, 78% report extremely serious consequences of error, 36% report very high responsibility for the health and safety of others, 48% face time pressure daily, and 52% encounter conflict situations more than weekly), and from the provisions of China's Measures for the Administration of Licensing for Special Maternal and Infant Health Care Technical Services and Personnel Qualifications and the Nurses Regulation on assessment qualification, critical condition reporting, and occupational health surveillance; control requirements should be tailored to the institution and local rules.

Midwifery personnel, obstetric physicians and nursing staff, and the newborn team are affected; no newcomer or night shift group comparison data was obtained this round, and it is not asserted that they are most likely to omit steps.

Possible consequences | delayed assessment or monitoring may lead to maternal and infant complications and poor outcomes; medication or procedure errors cause maternal and infant harm; inadequate newborn resuscitation preparation delays rescue; inadequate infection exposure protection affects occupational health; and missing records and follow-up affect care continuity and responsibility traceability.

Boundary statement two | providing midwifery technical services must be carried out within a licensed institution, and health technical personnel may not provide special maternal and infant health care technical services privately or in an institution that has not obtained the license.

Boundary statement three | occupational protection and health surveillance are continuing obligations: nurses engaged in work with infection risk enjoy occupational health surveillance rights in accordance with law, and institutions should provide protective equipment and implement post-exposure procedures.

Article 17 of China's Nurses Regulation: notify a physician immediately when the condition is critical, and necessary emergency rescue should be given first to save a dying patient; act according to ability, standards, and institutional plans, and do not mechanically wait for referral. Out-of-scope procedures such as surgery require initiating the applicable referral and team rescue, without expanding authority on one's own.

Capability progression should start with supervised learning of antenatal assessment, fetal heart monitoring, and delivery observation, then after obtaining practice registration, passing the midwifery technology assessment, and receiving institutional position authorization take on routine antenatal care and labor management, then participate in anomaly handling and obstetric emergency support, and finally enter mentoring, quality improvement, and guideline development; each step is premised on educational background, assessment qualification, institutional license scope, and position authorization.

items.answer: The daily closed loop centers on antenatal assessment and labor management: complete antenatal examinations and fetal monitoring → develop the health management and follow-up plan → assess labor progress and manage abnormalities → complete delivery and initial newborn assessment → postpartum observation and breastfeeding guidance → record and hand over to collaborators; escalate through the referral channel when beyond the scope of practice.

components.definition_block: Nurse Midwives (O*NET-SOC 29-1161.00, Nurse Midwives) diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birth process independently or within a medical team, and may provide gynecological care for healthy women; this occupation in the United States requires professional graduate nursing education. The work includes providing antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, and newborn care, monitoring fetal development by listening to fetal heart tones, external uterine measurement, identifying fetal position, and estimating fetal size, recording health history and physical examination findings, performing vital sign, reflex, breast, and pelvic examinations, prescribing medications within the scope permitted by state regulations, ordering and interpreting diagnostic or laboratory tests, providing family planning services and individualized health management plans, initiating emergency interventions to stabilize patients, consulting or referring to specialists when the condition exceeds the scope of practice or professional competence, educating patients and families about maternity and newborn care, writing narrative summaries in the medical record to convey patient information to other healthcare providers, and instructing student midwives, medical students, or residents; the actually executable scope is determined by license, certification, institutional licensing, and position authorization.

subject.summary: Nurse Midwives (O*NET-SOC 29-1161.00, Nurse Midwives) diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birth process independently or within a medical team, and may provide gynecological care for healthy women; this occupation in the United States requires professional graduate nursing education. The work includes providing antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, and newborn care, monitoring fetal development by listening to fetal heart tones, external uterine measurement, identifying fetal position, and estimating fetal size, recording health history and physical examination findings, performing vital sign, reflex, breast, and pelvic examinations, prescribing medications within the scope permitted by state regulations, ordering and interpreting diagnostic or laboratory tests, providing family planning services and individualized health management plans, initiating emergency interventions to stabilize patients, consulting or referring to specialists when the condition exceeds the scope of practice, educating patients, families, staff, and the community, and instructing student midwives and medical students. This page uses only official sources to explain the occupational scope, tasks, China-U.S. admission differences, and statistical scope.
